posts.name: dpt
posts.cooked:
Well, first off, it's clear that this is a deliberate choice on their part to tell the story out of order (as opposed to just not getting around to it). Of course, something could be both a deliberate choice and a missed opportunity.

But I also don't know whether or not it was a good choice on their part. It's obvious looking at even the base set that there's a really rich story behind all the characters, that there's much more going on than is revealed on the surface. I feel like this adds a lot to the game, even for casual players. Of course there are different degrees of this.

Some of the out-of-order storytelling is quite unusual, but other bits are more ordinary serial storytelling conventions. For instance, it's quite typical in fiction series that we don't know what's going to be happening in the final showdown. It's unusual that we have seen little hints of what might be happening. I know it's one standard fiction-writing technique to write little back vignettes for your characters that you don't share with the readers.

In the specific case of Mr. Fixer, I think his story is revealed pretty straightforwardly in the Temple of Zhu Long deck.

posts.name: Foote
posts.cooked:
Spiff:

I thing GtG has missed out by not sharing the game's story more directly than they have.  

The Letters Page podcast was supposed to fill this need. Unfortunatley that idea has been shelved indefinitely.

There is only so much we can infer from the art and text. Even little hints can be interpreted totally wrong or go unnoticed completley (for instance, my theory that Visionary was from the IL timeline originally was confirmed as totally wrong. Incidently this means there is a version of the Freedom 6 we have not yet seen). There are tons of small-ish storylines alluded to in-game we know nothing about (like for instance how Ra gets captured and is saved by Fanatic, or the entire Heliopolis War thing for that matter) where there is very little art/text to put together a narrative on our own.

 

As far as Chokepoint goes in your other question, here is what we know. She was evidently brought back to Ft Adamant in seceret after her supposed death at KNYFE's hands post the V5 uprising (see KNYFE's deck for artwork on this). Deadline's alien power crystal thing was evidently in their possesion as well, as they both merged and she gained cosmic-level visions/knowledge as a result.  She is now driven to, I guess, remake the world in an image she sees fit based upon her newfound knowledge and power. Given her ability to use and manipulate tech/metal/armor/whathaveyou, heros like Unity/AbZero/Bunker had to find new ways to combat her, leading to their Termi-nation promos.

posts.name: Rabit
posts.cooked:
Often an RPG is set in a world populated by characters that tell a story around the actions of the player characters (PCs). The story of the PCs might dip in and out of the story of other characters, but those other stories are happening around them, regardless. It really depends on the game / campaign setting, though.

Hopefully the RPG storyline will start at the end of the card game, as that will allow us to get all the card game's background and story, and set us at a point in time where we can do interesting things in the aftermath of the final set. Then we can learn the story of the world following the card game through the events described in the adventures they publish. 

(I thought they'd actually told us when the RPG was going to be set, but I can't find it nor can I remember. Anyone else have that?)
